thesis: The guest argues that portfolio concentration is a primary driver of success in venture capital because each win has a greater impact, provided the firm chooses well through a thoughtful process rather than relying on diversification. He further contends that track record is a lagging indicator rather than a leading one due to the long horizon of eight to eleven years for public exits and the financial law of levitation, where perceived early success makes raising subsequent, larger funds easier. Consequently, he suggests that size may be a contra-indicator to success, citing firms like Benchmark and First Round as examples of those who can maintain repeatability while staying within their fund range.
